messages:
Alyssa (Account Executive): Heads-up: Acme signed for a 30-day POC. They sent expected traffic: steady 12 rps, 20m windows at 25 rps, and rare bursts ~90 rps for ~3 minutes. p95 target <200ms. Need recommended provisioning, pricing line items, and security questionnaire answers.

Jin (Sales Engineer): What's the model family/size? 13B vs 70B matters a lot. Quantized variant available?

Alyssa (Account Executive): They're planning to run a 13B open model, will try our 4-bit quantized checkpoint for burst handling if we advise it.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): Quick capacity sketch: 12 rps steady on 13B non-quantized -> approx 1 A100-equivalent node with efficient batching. For 25 rps sustained, either autoscale to 2 nodes or reserve 2 GPUs. 90 rps bursts need prewarm/burst or fall back to quantized model (2-3x throughput). Important: token lengths?

Alyssa (Account Executive): Avg request ~1k tokens, ~5% long tails at ~5k tokens.

Marta (SRE): Long requests dominate GPU-seconds. Ops options:
- Dedicated-reserved: reserve 2 GPUs, autoscale floor 1/ceiling 3, keep 2 prewarm nodes to absorb 3m bursts.
- Hybrid: reserve 1 GPU, allow burst into shared capacity + route long jobs to reserved pool. Expect tail latency hits when shared used.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): Also enable KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts. We often see ~15-25% token/time savings for assistant-style sessions. That shifts effective capacity down.

Jin (Sales Engineer): Autoscale policy proposal:
- scale up when avg GPU util > 70% sustained for 30s
- scale down when < 35% for 2m
- keep 2 prewarm instances for burst handling
Map long (>3k tokens) to reserved-only queue.

Marta (SRE): Runbook snippet for POC load generator:
```
# local loadgen example
./loadgen --rps 12 --burst 90 --dist long:5% --avg-tokens 1000 --long-tokens 5000 --duration 2h
```
We'll run internal sim to validate.

Priya (Finance): Pricing sketch: reserved 2x A100-equivalent for 30d = quote line, burst minutes billed as overage at 1.5x if beyond reserved. Quantized variant reduces GPU time ~30% so include optional discount line. I'll produce numbers after we confirm token mix.

Alyssa (Account Executive): Security questionnaire items to confirm: customer-managed KMS, SOC2, VPC/private options. I need the quick answers to include in the RFP reply.

sec-bot (security-bot): Security answers: KMS (customer-managed) = supported, SOC2 Type II (2024) = yes, VPC/private deployment = available via Redwood Private. See internal doc: https://internal.redwood/security/poc-answers

Jin (Sales Engineer): Fallback strategy if we overload: 1) route to quantized-4bit variant (throughput x2-x3, latency +10-30%), 2) shed or defer long tails with notice, 3) degrade features (e.g., reduce sampling steps) as last resort. We'll codify routing priority: reserved -> quantized -> shared -> rate-limit.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): Also recommend token-budget throttles and optional early-stopping heuristics for POC to protect SLOs. Map client long requests to reserved pool only.

Marta (SRE): I'll prepare autoscale template and preheat config. Also on-call runbook: escalation steps, how to flip fallback routing, and where to adjust thresholds.

Priya (Finance): I'll draft the quote including: reserved 2 GPUs, burst headroom to 3, burst overage pricing, and optional quantized savings. ETA 24h.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): I'll run the sim tomorrow with Marta and post latency heatmaps and expected GPU-util curves.

Alyssa (Account Executive): Two asks to bring back to Acme: confirm 1) token mix (avg vs long) and 2) whether they'll accept quantized model for bursts. I'll ping them now and paste their reply here. :thumbsup:
